newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-BOC sale to fund core business.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BOC sale to fund core business.

text.p: British specialist gases company BOC Group Plc said on Wednesday proceeds from the planned sale of health business Ohmeda would be used to fund development of its core industrial gases operation.
Chief executive Danny Rosenkranz told Reuters in a telephone interview that the money "won't burn a hole in our pocket".
"Our plans are pretty much as they were. We have no big acquisitions in mind. We have a very aggressive investment programme in gases," he said.
Rosenkranz did not rule out acquisitions, saying BOC was constantly "looking for opportunities, but at this point in time we have no particular plans".
He also ruled out a sale of BOC's second underperforming business, the vacuum technology and distribution service arm which has been hit by a prolonged downturn in the U.S. semiconductor industry.
"There are no plans to sell any other parts," he said.
Rosenkranz told Reuters in May that the group's priorities included boosting the proportion of sales achieved in the Asia Pacific region, notably Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia.
The company invests heavily in gas production plants which have to be close customers because of transport problems, allowing a 15-year payback period on investments.

Rosenkranz said on Wednesday BOC had not held any talks with potential purchasers for Ohmeda, which is one of the world's leading producers of anaesthetic gas and critical monitoring equipment. A prospectus for buyers is to be issued shortly.

"We have always said we would evaluate this business and form a view on what we were going to do with it. The business is now at a crossroads. It had reached a point where it has been cleaned up, and it is much easier for a potential purchaser to look at it," he said.
He declined to comment on the type of business that might emerge as a purchaser for Ohmeda, or on the price/earnings multiple BOC was seeking.
Ohmeda, which accounted for less than 12 percent of group sales at the half-year stage, has been passing through a difficult period.
In the six months to March, sales dropped nine percent to 226.3 million stg and profits fell eight percent to 26.1 million stg, with the U.S. market particularly tough.
"BOC now has a choice - either to sell it...or put serious money into it," said Rosenkranz, adding that he preferred to put resources into the core industrial gases business.
He said Ohmeda was at a point where its oldest inhaled anaesthetic Forane had "stabilised" after being buffeted by generic competition since 1993.
Suprane, its newest anaesthetic was increasing market share, and a nitric oxide treatment for respiratory failure in new-born babies had been filed with U.S. regulators, Rosenkranz added.
